Does buying Apple's largest iPhone Pro get you the best camera features? The answer varies with each generation. To date, most reports have indicated that there will be no camera specification differences between the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, but today a leaker has cast some doubt on that claim.

Specifically, they said that two new features expected to be added to both Pro models "may" instead be exclusive to the Pro Max...

The iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max offer identical camera specifications, with all three rear cameras featuring 48-megapixel sensors. Apple says the telephoto lens offers up to 8x optical zoom, but this is achieved by cropping a 24-megapixel image, so the more accurate claim is 4x optical zoom with the option to output a cropped 8x image.

We've been expecting (for the most part) that both Pro models this year will maintain identical camera specifications, while both featuring a variable aperture main lens and a telephoto lens with a wider aperture for better low-light photography.

However, leaker Ice Universe said two new telephoto lens features could be exclusive to the iPhone 18 Pro Max.

If true, this means if you want the longest telephoto reach and the best low-light performance, you'll have to get the Pro Max model. However, the source used the word "may," suggesting they aren't entirely certain about this claim—perhaps seeing conflicting evidence in Apple's supply chain.

There are also reports that the variable aperture system on the main lens may be exclusive to the Pro Max, but reports on this have been inconsistent.

If you've always preferred the smaller of the two Pro models, would you upgrade to the Pro Max for better camera features? Let us know in the comments.
